intro_meme.prompt: A cartoon detective character standing in front of a giant blurry 42-piece jigsaw puzzle map of Texas, scratching his head, spotlighted on a stand-up stage.

outro_meme.prompt: The same detective character shrugging with a magnifying glass in hand, pointing toward a glowing 'READ MORE' sign.

sources.fact: Plains Cotton Growers represents 42 High Plains counties producing about 66% of Texas cotton and roughly 30% of the nation's.
USDA's Sept 14, 2026 disaster designation covers specific counties and additional contiguous eligible counties, but no county-by-county cotton loss data has been published yet.

lines.speaker: nate
lines.text: Kai, forty-two counties grow cotton up on the Texas High Plains.

screen.prompt: A cartoon patchwork quilt map made of 42 different county-shaped squares, all stitched together with a cotton-boll motif.

lines.voice_instructions: Channel Richard Pryor-style stand-up energy: exasperated, escalating, physically reactive delivery — real gasps, real disbelief, voice cracking on the big number. This is two friends losing it together over something absurd, not a news broadcast. Real cursing where the line calls for it, land every word of it like a punchline, not a warning label.
